proposal: TIER CONFIDENCE BY THE CLAIM'S QUANTIFIER (the ∀/∃ verification asymmetry). A PRESENCE claim (∃ — "here's the text/witness/data at line N") is reliable from a partial view: one accurate quote verifies it. An ABSENCE claim (∀ — "there is no X", "it never does Y", "it can't Z", "the falsifier is empty", "this store has 0 functional relations") is a universal requiring TOTAL coverage of the domain to verify — flag it PROVISIONAL until the whole domain (document/codebase/trajectory) is read or measured. Before asserting any "there is no / it never / it cannot", either cover the whole domain or explicitly grade the claim provisional-pending-full-coverage. This is the failure that cost the reviewer his sharpest finding (absence-claims survived 0/5); it's the reciprocal of 'verify source not label.' My own recent work is full of ∀-claims ("KG has 0 functional relations", "no maximal stream is posited", "percept_ft doesn't generalize") — each should carry a coverage caveat.
